It solves the problem of costly neighbor lookups required for gradient computation in sparse SDF storage (e.g., hash maps) by storing gradients directly, enabling efficient interpolation via first-order Taylor expansion without accessing multiple voxels [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that standard sparse SDFs (e.g., in hash maps) require costly neighbor lookups for gradient computation, particularly near block boundaries. It further explains that Gradient-SDF solves this by storing the gradient vector directly at each voxel. This allows for efficient interpolation and gradient estimation using a first-order Taylor expansion with only a single voxel lookup (via rounding), thereby avoiding the need to access multiple neighboring voxels.
